Hi Joe — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Summary of needs I heard: Elara needs a HIPAA-covered deployment, BAA execution, and access to SOC2 Type II evidence. You also mentioned periodic audits and a preference toward isolating PHI.
- Deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), Private VPC or on-prem (full isolation).

Questions / asks for you:
1) Can you confirm whether Elara requires Private VPC/on-prem for the initial POC, or whether Dedicated (with BAA) would be acceptable for a 3–6 month pilot?
2) Any specific SOC2 scope items we should pay attention to (e.g., audit log retention window, encryption KMS model, data residency requirements)?

Proposed next steps:
- I can send a redacted copy of our SOC2 Type II report and a BAA draft for legal to review (Marissa / Rishi, looping you in).
- If helpful, schedule a 30–45m security deep-dive next week to go over encryption, logging, and audit support.
- Draft mutual action plan / POC timeline (I attached a one-page MAP draft).

Do any of those next steps work for you? Two time options for the security deep-dive: Wed 3/3 9:00–10:00 PT or Thu 3/4 11:00–12:00 PT.

Subject: Re: Deployment mode and compliance follow-up (HIPAA / SOC2 / BAA)

Thanks, Dylan — great recap. Confirming a few details from our side: 

- Compliance posture: Elara is a HIPAA-covered entity. We will need a signed BAA before we ingest PHI into any third-party system. SOC2 Type II evidence is required for our security & procurement team (redacted copies are fine).
- Deployment preference: For the initial POC (3 months) our security team prefers Dedicated capacity in our cloud account or a Private VPC deployment. On-prem is a heavier lift for the POC but could be considered later. The deciding factor will be whether the Dedicated option includes: (a) BAA execution, (b) customer-controlled KMS or a FedRAMP-equivalent key management option, and (c) audit log retention of 12+ months accessible via API.
- Audits: We run annual third-party security assessments and will need to know how Redwood supports evidence collection (e.g., access to logs, sample configs, encryption attestations).

Next steps on our side: I'll route the BAA/requirements to procurement and security and share any specific legal redlines. Please send the SOC2 redacted report and the BAA draft. Also include any docs on key management and audit logging APIs.

Happy to take the security deep-dive on Wed 3/3 9am PT.

—Joe

Hi Joe — thanks for the clear list. Quick notes from Redwood Security/Legal: 

- SOC2: we can provide a redacted SOC2 Type II report (2026 audit period) for procurement. I will attach the redacted PDF in my next message.
- BAA: attached is our standard BAA draft. We're happy to work through redlines; please have your procurement/legal send suggested edits.
- KMS / keys: For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in the major cloud providers. For Private VPC deployments we can support customer KMS/HSM integration for encryption-at-rest.
- Audit logs: We retain control-plane audit logs for 18 months by default and can configure export windows; application-level request/response logs that include PHI must be disabled unless the customer requests and we put guardrails in the config and contract.
